quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good surface, you should:

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a good surface, leave it locked until you stop completely. Your motorcycle will stay under control on good pavement as long as it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal once you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about what you plan to do next.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Traction is poor on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement. Gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers also have poor traction.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can make the bike tip over. Use the rear brake instead to slow down safely during the turn.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a passenger vehicle's brake light.
questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as bright or noticeable as a car's brake light, especially when your taillight is on. Other drivers may not see your brake light, so be careful.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Inspecting the paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Wear leather boots that are high and sturdy. They protect your feet and ankles when riding.

questions.question: The human body removes alcohol at a rate of:
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Most people can remove the alcohol from about one drink per hour. This varies from person to person. The safest choice is to never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Good footing helps prevent your passenger from falling off and taking you with them.

questions.question: _________ of all collisions between motorcycles and cars are caused by drivers failing to yield the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of collisions between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers of larger vehicles will yield, even if they are supposed to by law.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Goes into your bloodstream right away

questions.correctAnswerText: Goes into your bloodstream right away
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine walls, enters your bloodstream, and reaches your brain quickly.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, if you crash. A windshield is not a good enough substitute.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:
questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the situation
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best, and no position should always be avoided. Change your lane position as needed based on conditions.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know they have seen you
It doesn't always mean they have actually seen you
They will yield to you properly

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they have actually seen you
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know a driver has seen you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not notice them.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, the center lane position is usually best for following a car. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better
Be comfortable, wearing shorts if it is hot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you better
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during broad daylight. Always wear brightly-colored clothes when riding, even during the day, so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: If your motorcycle does not trigger a traffic control device, what should you do?

options.text: Wait one complete cycle before yielding to other traffic and proceeding through the red light with caution
Back up and try again to trigger the signal
Flag down a police officer to report the light will not change

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait one complete cycle before yielding to other traffic and proceeding through the red light with caution
questions.explanation: A motorcycle may be too small to trigger some traffic signals. Wait for one complete light cycle, then proceed through the red light with caution. Yield to any traffic already in or approaching the intersection.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you
Sit as far back as possible
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to wait until after you start the engine before getting on. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: You should always check your blind spot before:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, merging onto a freeway, or passing.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a turn. If you turn too fast, you may drift out of your lane or leave the road.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while you are stopping, you should:

options.text: Continue to apply the front brake.
Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake immediately and then apply it firmly again. Use both brakes together if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best action is to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is usually safest, but this can change.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where to find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.
